medfit's native engine fits covariance-structure models, with observed intercepts and means, from
lavaan-style syntax.
It is not a replacement for lavaan: it covers the path models behind mediation
analysis and stops there. This page runs both on the same data, then lists what
each does, with a status for every feature that a test checks against a live
probe on each build.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Use medfit native when** | you want the indirect effect, `mbco_sem()`, or a nonlinear constraint such as `cp == a*b` on a path model |
| **Use lavaan when** | you need latent means, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators, broader FIML models, or fit indices |
| **Both** | read the same `~`, `=~`, `~~`, `:=` and constraint syntax, and agree to about 1e-6 where both apply |

## The same model in both

```{r}
#| label: both
library(medfit)
library(generics)
library(lavaan)
model <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment
  ab := a * b
"
native <- tidy(fit_sem(model, mediation_demo))
ref <- parameterEstimates(sem(model, mediation_demo))
rows <- native[native$term %in% c("a", "b", "cp", "ab"), ]
i <- match(rows$term, ref$label)
data.frame(term = rows$term, native = rows$estimate, lavaan = ref$est[i],
           se_native = rows$std_error, se_lavaan = ref$se[i])
```

Both fit with their defaults: lavaan fixes the exogenous covariates, and since medfit 0.15.0 so does
`fit_sem()` (`fixed_x` is the exogenous observed variables, `meanstructure` is `TRUE`). The standard
errors, including the delta-method error of `ab`, agree as well. Pass `fixed_x = FALSE` (and `fixed.x = FALSE`
in lavaan) to estimate the exogenous variances and covariances instead.

## Where they differ by design

The default information matrix is observed in medfit and expected in lavaan.
They agree for a well-fitting model and separate when the model is
misspecified; `information = "expected"` reproduces lavaan:

```{r}
#| label: information
bad <- "mediator1 ~ treatment\nmediator2 ~ treatment\noutcome ~ mediator1 + mediator2"
rbind(
  native_observed = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_sem(bad, mediation_demo))))[3],
  native_expected = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_sem(bad, mediation_demo, information = "expected"))))[3],
  lavaan = sqrt(diag(vcov(sem(bad, mediation_demo))))[3]
)
```

## Feature table

Status is one of **Supported** (matches lavaan where lavaan has it),
**Partial** (a subset), **Different by design** (both exist and differ on
purpose) and **Unsupported** (use lavaan). Each row is checked by
`tests/testthat/test-lavaan-comparison.R`; editing a status without changing
the behavior makes that test fail.

| Feature | lavaan | medfit native | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paths, covariances, labels, fixed values, bounds | yes | yes | Supported |
| Several modifiers on one term | yes | one per term | Unsupported |
| Means and intercepts | yes | observed intercepts and means (`y ~ 1`, `y ~ 1 + x`); latent means are planned | Supported |
| Multiple groups | yes | no | Unsupported |
| Estimators other than ML | yes | ML, plus the HC0 sandwich | Partial |
| Missing data | FIML | listwise by default; separate bounded random-X FIML opt-in | Partial |
| Categorical outcomes | WLSMV and others | numeric variables only; use lavaan (WLSMV) | Unsupported |
| Information matrix | expected | observed by default | Different by design |
| Robust standard errors | yes | `se_type = "sandwich"` equals lavaan's huber.white | Supported |
| Linear constraints | yes | yes | Supported |
| Nonlinear constraints | yes | yes, including `a*b > k` and sums of products | Supported |
| Defined parameters | `:=` | `:=` with delta-method errors | Supported |
| Chi-square and df | yes | `glance()` | Supported |
| CFI, RMSEA, SRMR | yes | not reported | Unsupported |
| logLik, AIC, BIC | yes | equal when both fit the same settings (the 0.15.0 defaults count the intercepts, as `meanstructure = TRUE` does in lavaan) | Supported |
| Standardized estimates, modification indices, fitted values, residuals | yes | no | Unsupported |
| Fixed exogenous covariates | `fixed.x = TRUE` is the default | `fixed_x = TRUE` or names, and `TRUE` is the default since 0.15.0; product columns are fixed with the rest; a statement on a selected variable is an error | Supported |
| Product terms (`x:m`) and four-way effects | `x:m` is an observed exogenous column, kept as written; no mediation effects | `x:m` stored as `m:x`; coefficients and sandwich standard errors equal lavaan's; `extract_mediation()` gives the four-way parts; chi-square, df and p-value are `NA` and `anova()`, `mbco_sem()` refuse when a factor is a regression target; a supported class only | Partial |
| Nested model comparison | `lavTestLRT()` | `anova()` | Supported |
| Mediation effects and the MBCO test | no | `extract_mediation()`, `mbco_sem()` | Supported |

The first column names the feature; the probe for a row is in the test, not
here, so the table cannot drift from the code without a failing test.

### Products, in both

lavaan reads `x:m` as an observed exogenous column and so does medfit, so the coefficients and the
sandwich standard errors agree, with `fixed.x = TRUE` as well as with `fixed.x = FALSE` (the product
column is fixed with the other exogenous variables):

```{r}
#| label: product-both
prod_model <- "mediator1 ~ treatment
               outcome_int ~ mediator1 + treatment + treatment:mediator1"
nat <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(prod_model, mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich", fixed_x = FALSE))
lav <- sem(prod_model, mediation_demo, fixed.x = FALSE, se = "robust.huber.white")
nat_fx <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(prod_model, mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich"))
lav_fx <- sem(prod_model, mediation_demo, fixed.x = TRUE, se = "robust.huber.white")
paths <- 1:4
rbind(
  max_diff_estimate = max(abs(coef(nat)[paths] - lavaan::coef(lav)[paths])),
  max_diff_se = max(abs(sqrt(diag(vcov(nat)))[paths] - sqrt(diag(lavaan::vcov(lav)))[paths])),
  max_diff_estimate_fixed_x = max(abs(coef(nat_fx)[paths] - lavaan::coef(lav_fx)[paths]))
)
```

They differ in what follows. lavaan reports a chi-square for this model; medfit reports `NA`, because
the product contains a regression target (`mediator1`) and the model treats it as exogenous, which makes
the global test invalid (see [the native model page](model-native.html#product-terms)). lavaan stores the
product under the spelling you wrote (`treatment:mediator1`); medfit stores `mediator1:treatment`, whichever
order you write. A model medfit rejects (a residual covariance between outcomes, a shared or fixed coefficient,
a constraint on a coefficient, a bound) is still fitted by lavaan.

## Checking a constrained LR against lavaan or OpenMx

The test of an indirect effect, $ab = 0$, can be posed to a general optimizer as the nonlinear constraint
`a*b == 0`. That is the one place where a general optimizer can return a wrong statistic without saying so: OpenMx
started at $a = b = 0$ can drop the constraint (its Jacobian is zero there), and lavaan can stop at a branch with a
larger statistic than the true minimum. medfit never poses that constraint to its own solver: `mbco_sem()` takes
the smaller of the two linear nulls. The decomposition is exact (the product is zero exactly when one factor is); each
branch is a numerical refit from several starts, so the reference is the best accepted refit, not a proof of a global
minimum. `compare_lr()` runs the nonlinear form in lavaan or OpenMx from two starts and compares it with medfit's
result. lavaan starts from its own default and from its `"simple"` start (the paths at 0); OpenMx starts from medfit's
default start and from the same start with the tested paths set to 0, the start at which it drops the constraint:

```{r}
#| label: compare-lr
#| eval: false
fit <- fit_sem("mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment", mediation_demo)
compare_lr(fit, paths = c("a", "b"), engine = "lavaan")
```

A warning is raised only on observed evidence, never because the engine's LR is zero (a valid fit has LR = 0 when
the unrestricted optimum already satisfies the null):

| Condition | Warning class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The engine's returned fit violates $ab = 0$ | `medfit_warning_engine_constraint_dropped` | $|ab|$ above `1e-4` in the natural units of the product |
| A feasible run's statistic exceeds medfit's best accepted refit | `medfit_warning_engine_statistic_above_max` | difference above `1e-4 * max(1, LR)` |

Both inherit from `medfit_warning_engine_comparison`. The verdict is `"unresolved"`, and neither side is blamed, when
medfit has no accepted reference, the engine's unrestricted fit differs from medfit's (parameters, estimates, or the
discrepancy), or a run failed or could not be checked. Only observed-variable models are compared. A saturated mean
structure (every intercept free) and `fixed_x` (all, a named subset or a lenient subset) are supported in both engines:
the fixed exogenous moments are written to the engine as fixed parameters at their sample values, and in OpenMx a fit
with a mean structure runs on the raw data of the rows the fit used. Latent variables, products, fixed or constrained
intercepts, weights, factors, other fixed or shared parameters, start and bound modifiers and constraints in the model
are refused by name. The live check behind these statements is the
`compare-lr` gate (`tests/sim/compare-lr-gate.R`), which runs the issue's cell through both engines and fails only
when `compare_lr()` mislabels.

The same simple model written in OpenMx and semopy syntax, next to medfit and lavaan, is on
[One model in medfit, lavaan, OpenMx and semopy](syntax-crosswalk.html).
